items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: I never did know his right name. All I know was Two Bits because I was small then, you know.

ctx.x: Who was the drummer Two Bits? Do you remember what his name was?

Yeah, Lloyd Two Bits. Yeah, he was around the Third War, too. I forgot to mention his name. What was his drummer? He was a pretty good little drummer. I never did know his right name. All I know was Two Bits because I was small then, you know. He had a pretty good edge on him then. But he was a pretty good little drummer, too. Then we had Cook Shop Son. He was another drummer.

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1969-03-24
items.q: well I had other little few drummers like a fella called Two Bits, Sun Shop, or Cook Shop Sun.

ctx.x: Okay, well we're interviewing Joe Watkins this March 24th, 1969. Just going from what you're about to say, Joe, about when you started music.

When I started, I started in 1920s. Well that was quite a few years after George Lewis and Paul Barbrain. Well I always did love drums because I was born in the third ward and that was, a section for jazz probably because Lee Armstrong was from that ward. He was born and raised around there. And I don't know about Joe Oliver because I always heard that Joe was not exactly from the Orlins. But it was him, Lee Armstrong, Funk Johnson, and you had Manuel Moneta. And, uh, was this other fella's name, uh, was a good…
What sort of date was this? Huh? What date was this about?

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: No, all I knew was Two Bits.

ctx.x: Had you played any other instruments first? Any like guitar? No, no other instruments.
I was just crazy about drums from a child when Baby Dots was playing in New Orleans at that time. Baby Dots, Henry Martin, Black Benny, Two Bits, and all those drummers.
Well tell me, I don't want to interrupt you all the time, but tell me about Two Bits. I know Bunk used to mention Two Bits, and I never heard anybody else mention it until you did.
